ezekiel.17.p1.b1.text: Son of man, pose a riddle; speak a parable to the house of Israel

ezekiel.17.p1.b2.text: A great eagle with great wings and long pinions, full of feathers of many colors, came to Lebanon and took away the top of the cedar.

ezekiel.17.p1.b3.text: He plucked off its topmost shoot, carried it to the land of merchants, and planted it in a city of traders.

ezekiel.17.p1.b4.text: It sprouted and became a spreading vine, low in height, with branches turned toward him

ezekiel.17.p1.b5.text: And behold, this vine bent its roots toward him. It stretched out its branches to him from its planting bed

ezekiel.17.p1.b6.text: Will it not completely wither when the east wind strikes?

ezekiel.17.p2.b1.text: He took a member of the royal family and made a covenant with him, putting him under oath.

ezekiel.17.p2.b2.text: But this king rebelled against Babylon by sending his envoys to Egypt to ask for horses and a large army. Will he flourish?

ezekiel.17.p2.b3.text: I will spread My net over him and catch him in My snare.

ezekiel.17.p2.b4.text: I will take a shoot from the lofty top of the cedar, and I will set it out. … I will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.

ezekiel.17.p2.b5.text: it will yield fruit and become a majestic cedar. Birds of every kind will nest under it

ezekiel.17.p2.b6.text: I bring the tall tree down and make the low tree tall. I dry up the green tree and make the withered tree flourish.
